subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should OpenClaw add a new observational `message:sending` internal-hook contract, or keep pre-send mutation and cancellation exclusively on typed plugin hooks?
rationale: Current public documentation defines internal hooks as coarse side-effect automation and typed plugin hooks as the policy surface; `message:sending` is not an established internal event, so adding it and choosing its timing creates a new security- and compatibility-sensitive core contract.

options.title: Keep pre-send policy typed-only
options.body: Do not add the internal event; direct filtering, rewriting, encryption, and cancellation use cases to typed `api.on("message_sending")` hooks.

options.title: Add a post-policy observer
options.body: Approve a colon-only internal event that receives the final non-cancelled payload immediately before channel delivery, with full docs, guard, diagnostics, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Adopt pre-policy alias semantics
options.body: Intentionally expose raw pre-policy content and both event spellings, accepting the duplicate-dispatch and long-term compatibility burden after explicit documentation and proof.

recommendation.title: Keep pre-send policy typed-only
recommendation.body: Do not add the internal event; direct filtering, rewriting, encryption, and cancellation use cases to typed `api.on("message_sending")` hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent maintainer PR already owns exactly-once `message_sending` placement and channel-delivery boundary analysis.
